claim: Meta-analysis of 74 VNS studies (3321 patients): seizure frequency reduced 36% at 3-12 months and 51% after >1 year; ~50% of patients had >=50% reduction at last follow-up; seizure freedom rarely achieved.

bibliographic_record.authors: Englot DJ, Chang EF, Auguste KI.
bibliographic_record.title: Vagus nerve stimulation for epilepsy: a meta-analysis of efficacy and predictors of response.

supporting_passage: The authors performed the first meta-analysis of VNS efficacy in epilepsy, identifying 74 clinical studies with 3321 patients suffering from intractable epilepsy. [...] After VNS, seizure frequency was reduced by an average of 45%, with a 36% reduction in seizures at 3-12 months after surgery and a 51% reduction after > 1 year of therapy. [...] At the last follow-up, seizures were reduced by 50% or more in approximately 50% of the patients [...] it is important to recognize that complete seizure freedom is rarely achieved using VNS and that a quarter of patients do not receive any benefit from therapy.
